newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - STG/MARK VOLS GAIN AS SPOT STG SINKS.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - STG/MARK VOLS GAIN AS SPOT STG SINKS.

text.p: Sterling/mark option vols were pushed higher at the European midsession as sterling spot shed around five pfennigs from morning levels.
Dealers said sterling options trade was busy across the board as demand for sterling downside protection accelerated on spot's failure this week to retest last week's multi-year highs.
"People are beginning to see this as the end of higher sterling cycle and we're see big demand for out-of-the-money sterling puts down to 2.80," said a UK bank options dealer.
One-month sterling volatility ticked up to 12.4/12.8 percent at midday Europe from 12.0/12.3 late Thursday in Europe.
The risk reversal, the difference in implied volatility of calls relative to puts, was skewed more deeply for sterling puts at 0.3/0.8 against 0.1/0.4 late Thursday.
Sterling/mark spot slipped to levels below 2.93 by the midsession, well below morning levels above 2.98 marks and well off this week's highs above 3.06.
Long liquidation amid indications that UK interest rates will be held steady after Thursday's Bank of England rate hike was the prime mover in the pound's decline across the board.
Cable also sank, testing 10-month lows by midday Europe, but the options reaction was relatively muted.

"Vols have picked up and the risk reversal is bid more for sterling puts but we've already seen buying of sterling puts, people seem more prepared for it," said a U.S. bank dealer. "When it gets down to $1.55 is when we'll see vols really accelerating higher."
One-month sterling/dollar volatility was trading at 10.7/11.0 percent, up from late Thursday's 10.2/10.6. The risk reversal was a shade deeper into pound put territory at 0.3/0.7.
Spot cable slipped below $1.57 from levels above $1.59 in early trade and over $1.63 earlier in the week.
Elsewhere, dollar/mark vols were slightly easier with spot ranging below this week's highs. One-month vol was trading at 11.0/11.3 percent from 11.25/11.55 Thursday.
Dollar/yen was weaker, dipping below the 118 yen support area but vols were relatively unscathed with the one-month at 11.0/11.2 percent against 11.0/11.5.
